brief: Bear Traps frames a 1980s-style slowdown: a hot economy with rising rates and inflation squeezing the middle class while AI-driven wealth effects prop up GDP. Hot CPI/PPI prints (services +0.3% M/M, shelter +0.3%) plus a strong prior jobs report put Fed hike odds near 85% for next Wednesday, with the market now pricing two hikes for the rest of 2026; the yield curve flattened sharply after the CPI print and 30yr yields hit their highest level since 2007. Consumer spending is concentrated: the top 10% of earners drive roughly a third of GDP, backed by a record 48% equity share of household financial assets, so an AI scare (Dario Amodei's slowdown call, OpenAI's IPO delay to 2027) that dents that wealth effect could push recession odds from the mid-teens/low-20s toward 70%. Hyperscaler debt is framed as a repricing risk to the long end, not a default risk, if AI revenue growth stalls. Separately, China's 1.4-billion-barrel crude stockpile and a US SPR near its 1983 low give Beijing a CPI lever into the September 24 summit, while investment-grade and CCC credit are deteriorating together, which the note reads as a leading signal for equities.
